summary: Describes how L2TP is carried over Frame Relay, using permanent and switched virtual circuits. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: L2TP is a way to tunnel connections. This explains how to run it over an older leased-line network.

how does l2tp use frame relay pvc and svc
subtitle: How to carry L2TP-tunneled PPP sessions directly over Frame Relay virtual circuits instead of IP and UDP.

tldr.problem: L2TP was specified to run over IP and UDP, but some networks connect the tunnel endpoints with a Frame Relay network and need a defined way to carry L2TP there.
tldr.mechanism: L2TP packets are wrapped in a Q.922 Frame Relay frame with SNAP encapsulation, using NLPID 0x80, OUI 0x00-00-5E and PID 0x0007 to mark the payload as L2TP.
tldr.outcome: A LAC and an LNS can build tunnels over Frame Relay PVCs or SVCs, with minimum MTU rules and no changes to Frame Relay signaling. Security is deferred to the base L2TP specification.

today: RFC 3070 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the base L2TP specification, RFC 2661.

sections.title: Why L2TP Needs a Frame Relay Mapping
sections.content:
The Layer Two Tunneling Protocol (L2TP, RFC 2661) tunnels Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) sessions. It is designed to be independent of the media it runs over. The base specification describes how to run it over UDP and IP.

RFC 3070 describes how to run L2TP over native Frame Relay, on both Permanent Virtual Circuits (PVCs) and Switched Virtual Circuits (SVCs). Its applicability statement limits it to Frame Relay point-to-point circuits.
sections.plainLanguage: L2TP can travel over different kinds of networks. This document explains how to make it travel over one older kind, Frame Relay.

sections.title: The LAC, the LNS and the Tunnel
sections.content:
A user reaches the network through the PSTN or ISDN. An L2TP Access Concentrator (LAC) attaches to that switched network and passes traffic across a Frame Relay cloud to an L2TP Network Server (LNS), which terminates PPP and connects to LANs.

L2TP is connection-oriented. A session is created when an end-to-end PPP connection is attempted between a user and the LNS. A tunnel is defined by an LNS-LAC pair and carries the PPP datagrams for its sessions. The LAC need only implement the media over which L2TP runs, and it may tunnel any protocol carried within PPP.
sections.plainLanguage: The tunnel is a private pipe between two machines. Many people's calls can share the same pipe, and each call is a session inside it.

sections.title: Encapsulation and Frame Format
sections.content:
L2TP MUST be able to share a Frame Relay virtual circuit with other protocols. So every frame must say what it carries. All protocols on the circuit MUST encapsulate their packets within a Q.922 frame, and the L2TP frame format MUST be SNAP encapsulation as defined in RFC 1490 and FRF.3.1.

  • NLPID: the single octet 0x80, which indicates a SNAP header follows.
  • OUI: the three octets 0x00-00-5E, identifying IANA.
  • PID: 0x0007. IANA administers the meaning of the PID, and together the OUI and PID identify L2TP.

The L2TP packet follows, then the frame check sequence (FCS). The Q.922 control field is 0x03.
sections.plainLanguage: Each frame gets a label saying it holds L2TP, so the receiver knows how to open it. Different kinds of mail can then share one road.

sections.title: MTU Considerations
sections.content:
If Frame Relay fragmentation (FRF.12) is not supported, the two Frame Relay endpoints MUST support an MTU of at least 1526. That figure adds the PPP Max-Receive-Unit size, the PPP header size, the maximum L2TP header size and the Frame Relay header size.

To avoid packet discards on the Frame Relay interface, the RECOMMENDED default Frame Relay MTU is 1564, based on a PPP default MRU of 1500. How to ensure these settings is left to the implementation. Quality of service is out of scope: the RFC says QoS can be provided by proprietary mechanisms local to the LAC or LNS.
sections.plainLanguage: Frames have a maximum size. The envelope has to be big enough for the biggest letter plus all the extra labels, or it gets thrown away.

sections.title: How Frame Relay and L2TP Interact
sections.content:
For SVCs, connection setup is triggered when L2TP tries to create a tunnel. The triggering mechanism is left to the implementation, and there SHALL NOT be any change in Frame Relay SVC signaling. The tunnel endpoints MUST be identified by X.121 or E.164 addresses.

For PVCs, the circuit MAY be configured administratively, and the tunnel endpoints MUST be identified by the DLCI assigned to the PVC at configuration time. In both cases the address or DLCI MAY be obtained as tunnel endpoints for a user as defined in RFC 2868.

There SHALL be no framing issues between PPP and Frame Relay. The LAC strips the CRC, link framing and transparency bytes from PPP frames, encapsulates them in L2TP and forwards them over the Frame Relay tunnel.
sections.plainLanguage: On a permanent line the two ends are wired up in advance. On a dial-up style line, asking for a tunnel makes the network set up the connection, without changing how that setup works.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says there was no standard specification for Frame Relay security at the time, although the Frame Relay Forum was working on a Frame Relay Privacy Agreement. Security would be re-examined later to see whether protection specific to L2TP over Frame Relay is still required.

In the interim, the basic security issues are those discussed in the base L2TP specification.
sections.plainLanguage: This document does not add any new locks. It points to the locks already described for L2TP and says it will look again later.
